rollout_excluded: Attention rollout is not an input here. It is a function of the shared trunk's attention weights and carries no head axis (ADR 0008), so it cannot speak to whether two heads differ; nine identical matrices would read as agreement where the quantity has no head to vary over.
stored_not_analysed_note: The ISM archive stores all nine heads because one forward pass returns them all. Only `heads` are analysed here, and no agreement figure, pair or verdict covers the rest.

head_coverage.note: A head's own measured coverage on the Testset, which is a different population from the analysis intersection and different for each head. It is named apart so an intersection figure is never read as a coverage figure; no coverage count equals the intersection's row count.

agreement_definition: Spearman rank correlation between two heads' position profiles, taken within the named position range. `per_row` correlates the two profiles of a single row and summarises the distribution over the stratum's rows; `mean_profile` correlates the stratum's two mean profiles, one number per pair. The two answer different questions and neither replaces the other: a stratum can hold rows that disagree pairwise while its means align.
profile_definition: mean |ISM delta| over a position's three alternative bases, per row, position and head; the reference base's slot is a true zero and is excluded from the mean

single_head_profile.note: ISM was swept over the analysis intersection, so a per-head profile here is an intersection figure even though a single head's absolute numbers may use its own coverage elsewhere. `head_coverage` carries those counts under their own population name.

pooling_note: One entry per stratum and no combined entry. The two strata answer different questions over differently-shaped populations: generalisation is sequence generalisation on unseen protospacers, pam_library is a PAM experiment on 5 targets. Adding their row counts would add a sample size to a replication factor.
nan_policy_note: A correlation is undefined, not zero, where a profile is constant over the range; such rows are counted as `undefined_rows` and left out of the distribution, and a single undefined number is written as null. No field holds NaN.
interpretation_limit: Attribution describes the model's internal information use. No figure here is a claim about physical DNA/protein interaction, and a position the model is insensitive to may still matter biologically.

pam.width_note: This range spans too few positions for a rank correlation to be informative — over three positions the statistic can only take ±1, ±0.5 or 0, and a tie decides it. It is reported for completeness. The PAM question is answered by `pam_separation`, which works at base resolution over every row instead of ranking three positions.

pam_separation.position_share_definition: a head's mean sensitivity at positions 25-26 divided by its mean over the whole 30bp window, per row. A **profile shape**, defined on every row whatever its own PAM, and scale-free so the heads' sixfold different dynamic ranges do not decide the comparison. It is not an NGG-only quantity; `g_loss_share` is.
pam_separation.direction_share_definition: share of rows where SpCas9's sensitivity share strictly exceeds SpCas9-NG's. 1.0 is full separation in the direction the PAM requirement predicts; 0.0 means it never exceeds it, which includes the heads reading the positions identically. `paired_difference.share_negative` is the share running the other way.
pam_separation.separated_definition: the median paired symmetric relative difference of the two heads' 25-26 sensitivity shares reaches `relative_margin`. A reporting convention, not a significance test; the summaries are in this artifact so another margin can be applied to them. It is a claim about **magnitude only** — see `direction_consistent`.
pam_separation.direction_consistent_definition: the contrast runs in the predicted direction on at least `direction_consistent_share` of rows. Separate from `separated`, and the stricter claim: a stratum can separate on the median while a sizeable minority of its rows order the other way, and one boolean covering both would hide that.

discriminating_position.why: SpCas9 requires NGG and SpCas9-NG accepts NGA, so the two recognition rules differ at position 26 alone — both require G at 25. This is the only position where the heads' rules disagree, so the contrast is reported here as well as over 25-26.

pam_separation.g_loss_definition: -(mean delta over the non-G substitutions at positions 25-26) divided by the row's mean window sensitivity, on NGG rows only. Positive means losing the GG lowers the prediction.
pam_separation.reading: Separation would show the shared trunk specialising its PAM reading per head. No separation is equally a result: it says the shared trunk reads the PAM positions alike for both heads, and it is reported as a finding rather than treated as a bug or resolved by lowering the margin.

pam_base_sensitivity.definition: mean |ISM delta| over the stratum's rows at each PAM position and base, per head, on the fraction scale. The base-resolution PAM table ADR 0007 assigns to ISM rather than IG, since a single-base substitution is indifferent to the 6-mer token boundary that merges the PAM with the right flank.
pam_base_sensitivity.reference_slot_note: A base's cell averages over the rows where it is the reference base too, and there its delta is a **true zero** - substituting a base for itself changes nothing. So a low or zero cell at a position whose reference is that base is an artifact of the layout, not a finding that the model ignores the base: in an all-NGG population G at 25 and 26 reads exactly 0 for that reason.

single_head_profile.definition: mean |ISM delta| over a position's three alternative bases, per row, position and head; the reference base's slot is a true zero and is excluded from the mean

pam_library.qualifier_note: This stratum's rows are PAM variants of 5 protospacers, so its n is 5 targets rather than its row count, and the row count is never added to the other stratum's. Every figure in this entry is pooled over those variants: `rows` is the variant count, and the quantiles in `agreement` and `pam_separation` are quantiles over variants of 5 targets, not over 5 independent observations. `per_target` repeats the window agreement and the PAM contrast target by target, which is the breakdown a library-stratum finding is reported with — a contrast that holds on the pool but on only two of the five targets is a different result from one that holds on all five.
